filings.business_description: The company sells automotive parts, accessories, and maintenance items primarily to individual consumers and commercial customers. It operates a network of stores and distribution centers to provide these products and services. The business model focuses on offering quality merchandise and superior customer service to drive sales and customer loyalty.
filings.risk_factors_summary: The company faces several material risks including regulatory changes affecting trade tariffs, competitive pressures from other retailers, and macroeconomic factors such as inflation and consumer spending. Additionally, technological advancements and the increasing prevalence of electric vehicles may impact demand for traditional automotive parts. Supply chain disruptions and labor market challenges also pose significant risks to operations.
filings.mda_highlights: Management highlights that revenue growth has been driven by increases in same-store sales and the opening of new stores, with a compounded annual growth rate of approximately eight percent over the past five fiscal years. Key challenges include managing inventory costs, adapting to competitive pressures, and ensuring effective store expansion. The company emphasizes the importance of hiring and retaining qualified employees to maintain service quality and operational efficiency.

URL: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/autozone-q4-earnings-beat-estimates-135200571.html
**AutoZone, Inc.** AZO reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings per share of $56.05, which increased 15.1% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $54.54 by 2.8%. Net sales rose 5.6% to $6.60 billion but missed the consensus mark of $6.69 billion by 1.4%. Total company same-store sales increased 1.5% on a constant-currency basis. Domestic same-store sales increased 1.6% in the 16-week quarter. International same-store sales advanced 10.7% on a reported basis, while constant-currency growth was 1.3%, reflecting the impact of currency movements. Total company same-store sales rose 2.7% on a reported basis. Domestic commercial sales reached $1.91 billion, up 8.6% from the year-ago quarter. URL: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/autozone-nyse-azo-misses-q3-114005433.html
Auto parts and accessories retailer AutoZone (NYSE:AZO) fell short of the market's revenue expectations in Q3 CY2026, but sales rose 5.6% year on year to $6.59 billion. * **Free Cash Flow Margin:** 10.4%, up from 8.2% in the same quarter last year. * **Locations:** 8,031 at quarter end, up from 7,657 in the same quarter last year. * **Same-Store Sales** rose 2.7% year on year (4.5% in the same quarter last year). Over the last eight weeks of the quarter our sales results strengthened, and we feel we are well positioned for sales growth in fiscal 2027. As you can see below, AutoZone grew its sales at a tepid 5.2% compounded annual growth rate over the last three years, but to its credit, it opened new stores and increased sales at existing, established locations. This quarter, AutoZone's revenue grew by 5.6% year on year to $6.59 billion, missing Wall Street's estimates. In the latest quarter, AutoZone's same-store sales rose 2.7% year on year.

citations.claim: AutoZone distributes automotive replacement parts across the United States, Mexico and Brazil.
citations.excerpt: AutoZone distributes automotive replacement parts across the United States, Mexico and Brazil. At Q3 FY2026 it operated 6,766 U.S. stores, 933 in Mexico and 157 in Brazil; quarterly sales were $4.841B and domestic commercial sales grew 10.4%. The core U.S. advantage is urgent local availability created by dense stores, hubs and mega hubs, distribution centers, and commercial delivery coverage.

citations.claim: ROIC is consistently above 15% for the past four years.
The core advantage is a dense store footprint paired with a hub/mega-hub and distribution-center network that improves local parts availability and speed.
citations.excerpt: The core advantage is a dense store footprint paired with a hub/mega-hub and distribution-center network that improves local parts availability and speed for both DIY and commercial customers.
